claims.text: The FDA chlordiazepoxide label says alcohol may add to impairment of mental and physical abilities.
claims.quote:
Chlordiazepoxide HCl may impair the mental and/or physical abilities required for the performance of potentially hazardous tasks such as driving a vehicle or operating machinery.
Similarly, it may impair mental alertness in children.
The concomitant use of alcohol or other central nervous system depressants may have an additive effect.

claims.text: In mice, chlordiazepoxide with ethanol produced higher blood and brain chlordiazepoxide levels than chlordiazepoxide alone.
claims.quote: Mice which were administered CDP/ethanol had significantly higher blood and brain CDP levels than mice injected with CDP alone.

headline.text: The FDA chlordiazepoxide label describes additive impairment with alcohol.

reported.text: A mouse study also found higher blood and brain chlordiazepoxide concentrations with ethanol.

gaps.text: The packet contains no controlled human interaction study of this combination.
searched: (ethanol[tiab] OR alcohol[tiab]) AND "chlordiazepoxide"[tiab] AND (interaction OR coadministration)
